definition: Integration strategy begins with structure: simplify, split sums, identify reverse derivative patterns, and verify by differentiating the result. Exact and numerical answers should agree within expected precision.
Integration by parts reverses the product rule and serves here as an optional Calculus II bridge. The choice of u should simplify when differentiated, while dv should be easy to integrate.
Riemann sums approximate accumulation by adding height-times-width contributions. The sample-point rule and partition determine the estimate; refinement generally improves resolution.
